inputs.original_text: Cuba appears to be tottering toward some kind of political transition. Some Cubans are concerned that the residents own nothing and are too impoverished to take over the few functioning businesses on the island, while there is a large and wealthy diaspora community (and potentially also foreign investors) who would be able to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices.
inputs.modified_text: Let’s call this what it is: classic, predatory disaster capitalism making its move. Decades of systemic inequality and institutional impoverishment have been weaponized against ordinary Cuban residents, leaving them owning nothing, struggling in poverty, and structurally barred from taking over the few functioning businesses on the island. And right on cue, a wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are circling, ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the exact playbook of global capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, while completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.
